China Tech Hardware Trade Posts Stable Growth in May as Exports Edge Up

BEIJING, June 14—China’s technology hardware industry reported steady trade activity in May, with both exports and imports showing modest gains amid resilient global demand, according to official customs data released Friday.

Exports of technology hardware—including computers, telecommunications equipment, and semiconductor components—reached $48.7 billion last month, marking a 3.2% increase from the previous year. Imports in the sector rose 2.8% year-on-year to $34.9 billion, as manufacturers sourced components and raw materials to meet production schedules.

The figures reflect the continued importance of the tech hardware sector to China’s export economy, even as manufacturers navigate shifting demand patterns and evolving supply chain strategies. “The stable trade performance demonstrates the industry’s adaptability and the ongoing strength of global markets for Chinese technology products,” said Li Wenhua, an analyst at the China Electronics Trade Association.

The data showed a particularly strong performance in exports of consumer electronics, which rose 4.5% year-on-year. Exports of networking equipment, including routers and base stations, climbed 2.6%. Computer hardware shipments remained broadly steady, up 1.9% from May 2023.

According to the Ministry of Commerce, the sustained export growth was supported by steady orders from Southeast Asia and the Middle East, as well as moderate demand in Europe and North America. “We continue to see robust interest from our partners in ASEAN countries,” said Zhang Min, spokesperson for the ministry. “This is helping to offset softer demand in some traditional markets.”

On the import side, China’s purchases of semiconductor chips and related components saw a 3.4% gain, attributed in part to ongoing investments in domestic production capacity and efforts to strengthen supply chain resilience. The China Technology Hardware Manufacturers’ Union said the sector’s stable growth reflected “sound fundamentals and effective coordination across the supply chain.”

Several industry sources noted that shipping and logistics operations remained normal, with no significant disruptions reported in May. Mainland ports handled hardware shipments efficiently, industry officials said, while inventories remained within historical norms.

“Production schedules are being maintained, and there is no significant backlog in orders or shipments,” said Lin Qiang, operations manager at Yantai Digital Devices, a leading manufacturer in Shandong province. “Our clients in South America and Africa continue to place steady orders.”

Economists expect China’s technology hardware trade to remain steady in the coming months, supported by ongoing digitalization efforts globally. “We foresee continued moderate growth, barring any external shocks,” said Li Wenhua. “The fundamentals remain strong.”
